episodes.title: Three shots in a Bombay bedroom.

blocks.text: 27 April 1959, 4:30 PM. Commander Kawas Manekshaw Nanavati walked into Prem Ahuja’s bedroom at Jeevan Jyot apartments in Colaba, Bombay. Moments later, three shots rang out. Ahuja lay dead in a puddle of blood.

FACTUAL MATRIX (Statement of Facts): 27 April 1959, 4:30 PM. Commander Kawas Manekshaw Nanavati walked into Prem Ahuja’s bedroom at Jeevan Jyot apartments in Colaba, Bombay. Moments later, three shots rang out. Ahuja lay dead in a puddle of blood. The legal controversy originated from whether the act committed fell within the statutory exceptions.

episodes.kicker: EPISODE 07 · THE HIGH COURT & SUPREME COURT
episodes.title: Jury Overturned: Convicted of Murder.

blocks.text:
The 9-member jury had acquitted Nanavati by an 8-1 majority. But Sessions Judge Mehta found the verdict perverse and referred it to the Bombay High Court.

The High Court overturned the jury verdict, finding Nanavati guilty of murder under Section 302 IPC and sentencing him to life imprisonment. The Supreme Court dismissed his appeal in 1961.

episodes.title: The Four-Part Test & The Death of Jury Trials.

blocks.text:
Justice K. Subba Rao laid down the landmark 4-part test for Grave & Sudden Provocation:
1. The provocation must be grave and sudden.
2. The test is objective: would a reasonable person lose self-control?
3. Words and gestures can constitute provocation only in exceptional cases.
4. The fatal act must be committed before cooling time has elapsed.

Public outrage over jury bias in this case led Parliament to abolish jury trials in India in the 1973 CrPC.

episodes.title: चार सूत्रीय सिद्धांत और जूरी व्यवस्था का अंत।

blocks.text:
न्यायमूर्ति के. सुब्बा राव ने गंभीर और अचानक उकसावे के लिए 4 सूत्रीय ऐतिहासिक सिद्धांत तय किए:
1. उकसावा गंभीर और अचानक होना चाहिए।
2. पैमाना वस्तुनिष्ठ है: क्या एक सामान्य व्यक्ति आत्म-नियंत्रण खो देता?
3. केवल असाधारण मामलों में ही शब्द उकसावा बन सकते हैं।
4. कृत्य गुस्सा शांत होने (Cooling Time) से पहले होना चाहिए।

flashcards.q: Which court decided The Nanavati Case and in what year?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court of India in the year 1961.

flashcards.q: What was the primary legal issue addressed in this case?
What is the core Ratio Decidendi of the judgment?
flashcards.a: The Supreme Court upheld the High Court conviction under Section 302 IPC. The 3-hour interval between confession and the shooting provided sufficient cooling time, negating sudden provocation.

flashcards.q: What is the primary citation for this ruling?
flashcards.a: K.M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1962 SC 605, 1962 SCR Supl. (1) 567

flashcards.q: What is the current legal status of this precedent?
flashcards.a: Leading Indian authority on grave and sudden provocation and cooling-off periods.
